key_insight: HPDPO solves finite-horizon control without model derivatives by combining forward rollouts with a Hamiltonian primal-dual update to estimate future cost structure.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for control systems with reliable simulators but nonsmooth, learned, or black-box dynamics where gradients are unavailable or unstable.
method: Represent control as a finite-horizon time-indexed policy.
Evaluate candidate actions using deterministic suffix rollouts of the transition model.
Use a regularized Hamiltonian dual formulation with block-coordinate multiplier updates instead of differentiating dynamics or a critic.
evidence_signal: The method is validated on exact/nonsmooth benchmarks, a biomarker cascade, an amyloid Neural ODE from ADNI data, and three multidimensional control problems, where it closely matches reference objectives, trajectories, and controls.
watch_item: Performance depends on having a reliable forward simulator and may be sensitive to rollout horizon, multiplier regularization, and block-update tuning.
paper_title: Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Policy Reinforcement Learning for Derivative-Free Model-Based Control
